newsitem.title: INDIA: India best growth/valuation in Asia - Morgan Stanley.
newsitem.headline: India best growth/valuation in Asia - Morgan Stanley.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Asia said on Monday it remained confident on the outlook for India and had maintained the firm's overweight position on the country while reducing weightings in Malaysia and Thailand.
"The Indian market has the best growth/valuation relationship in the Asian theatre," Morgan Stanley said in a statement.

Morgan Stanley's team of analysts said this was because political turmoil in India had eased, the economic reform philosophy of most political groups was generally consistent and the budget for financial year 1998 (April-March) was market friendly.
They forecast a pickup in the global economy from around 3.5 percent to four percent this year and anticipated this will lead to a rebound in demand for many core cyclical industries.
"The portfolio emphasis continues to be on those Asian markets which are dominated by 'smokestack industries'," the statement added.

"The strengthening of the US dollar affecting south-east Asian countries, the rising US interest rate prospects and the general slowing economies and earnings in the southern part of the Asian region are the other major factors influencing the tilt in Morgan Stanley's Asia-Pacific model toward the northern part of the region and India," it said.
The Indian rupee has stayed strong against the dollar, and the Reserve Bank of India has had to intervene heavily to stop it appreciating further.
Morgan Stanley is a global financial services firm and one of the largest global custodians in India, with more than $1.2 billion in assets under custody.
